designationHistory.indexText: Natalie Peters Webster and her mother, Natalie Wells Peters, donated their roughly 200-acre family estate in Islip, Long Island, to the federal government in 1968 as a sanctuary for birds and other wildlife, which became Seatuck National Wildlife Refuge.

authority.citation: Donation to the Fish and Wildlife Service

designationHistory.note: Pass A (fws.gov: acquired in 1968 as a donation from the Peters family) and Pass B (Seatuck Environmental Association: the 200-acre estate was donated in 1968 for an "inviolate sanctuary") agree on the 1968 donation. The association says the property was "eventually" established as a refuge, so the formal designation could postdate the gift; no separate designation date was found.
